claygraph.delta: Test context-bound fast/slow binding with provenance-diverse reversal promotion. Preserve previous binding versions instead of overwrite. Do not apply dynamic propagation to exact identity queries by default.

claycode.delta: Attempt to express ContextRef, provenance-family identity, binding validity/version, SHADOW promotion, conflict/unknown, rollback and promotion receipts using current G9 IR/type/effect semantics. Do not add syntax unless an executable counterexample demonstrates insufficiency.

harness.delta: When H1 becomes available, add true reversal vs duplicate-echo vs context bifurcation vs source-family spoof vs single-authoritative-source vs out-of-order replay arms to H-WP-06/H-WP-12, with gate lesion/rescue and rollback/rebuild.

unifieddb.delta: Persist source/provenance-family identity, semantic/source epoch, binding version validity and promotion/rollback receipts transactionally. Repeated rows/copies must not imply independent provenance.

frank.delta: Repeated loop activation or re-entry must not automatically consolidate a slow ClayGraph binding. Durable relation reversal needs independently qualified evidence/outcome credit or an exact authoritative update path.

hyperposition.delta: When contradiction is explained by context, preserve simultaneous context-specific alternatives rather than collapsing to one global edge; topology switching remains reversible and separately authorized.

gwt.delta: RAB is upstream graph-memory state. Graph exposure/promotion is not receiver uptake, causal use, outcome or recurrence authority. Existing R8 trajectory/receiver boundaries remain unchanged.

emergenz.delta: Treat repeated/coactivated evidence from one ancestry family as a source-echo/common-driver confound. Any causal claim for a binding still needs intervention/lesion/rescue/shuffle/OOD evidence beyond RAB selection performance.

clayresearch.delta: Fast/slow state is useful only conditionally. The constructed RAB test shows a stability/plasticity Pareto frontier: source-echo robustness improves strongly, while high-noise adaptation can worsen. Preserve matched-cost comparisons rather than promoting richer state universally.
